title.narrative: UN-HABITAT – IUTC Partnership to develop Local Government Capacities in the Asia-Pacific Region

description.narrative:
UN-Habitat and Gangwon State agreed to extend the long-standing partnership which began in 2007 to support the International Urban Training Centre (IUTC) by five more years (2023-27). A Memorandum of Understanding and Contribution Agreement to this effect was signed in May 2023. The collaboration entails a financial contribution of approximately USD 1,300,000 over the said period.
The project aims to improve the capacity of targeted local governments and their partners in Asia and the Pacific region to respond to sustainable urban development challenges. Two outcomes have been identified: 1) Targeted local government officials and their partners are able to demonstrate increased knowledge in sustainable urban development concepts and methodologies, and 2) The IUTC’s institutional capacity to carry out quality capacity-building programmes on sustainable urban development is strengthened.
Outcome 1 is expected to be achieved primarily through the delivery of six international training programmes annually on urban sustainability. The programmes will be well-tailored based on training needs assessment. Relevant follow-ups will be offered to support projects proposed by participants during the training. UN-Habitat knowledge and tools as well as Korean expertise will be integrated into the training programmes. Targeted training participants will mostly be government officials in the technical cadres with opportunities to also be forwarded to urban professionals working on local-level projects (i.e. “local government’s partners”).
Outcome 2 is expected to be achieved through strengthened engagement between UN-Habitat, Gangwon State as the donor, and the IUTC as the Implementing Partner. It will provide a platform to co-create an improved operational plan. International and regional networks will additionally be leveraged to enhance IUTC programmes. A strengthened collaboration with the Regional Office of Asia Pacific is also envisioned through the partnership.
COVID-19 has posed a challenge in the previous phase of the partnership but has also provided an opportunity to integrate a higher-quality online and digital learning component into IUTC programmes. In this phase of the collaboration, we will try to address both this challenge and opportunity. Additionally, this phase should encourage a joint reflection and understanding on developing IUTC as a Centre of Excellence in the region.
